mainEntity.name: How do I decide between moving and building a home addition for more space?

acceptedAnswer.text: A home addition is the better option when you require tailored square footage, want to preserve vehicle storage, and wish to stay in your existing neighborhood. Moving involves significant real estate fees, closing expenses, and moving logistical costs. Building an addition lets you expand a primary suite, family area, or in-law suite while matching your existing exterior stucco and architectural lines. However, if your lot lacks adequate setback clearance or municipal lot coverage limits prevent expanding outward, finding a larger property may be the only feasible alternative.
acceptedAnswer.description: Build an addition to avoid moving costs and keep your neighborhood if your lot allows expansion; move if property boundaries or zoning lot limits prevent adding square footage.
